name: Example: Orientation-Dependence
problem: If $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= 8$ and $\displaystyle\int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= -2,$ calculate $\displaystyle\int_{-C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x$ given that $C = C_1\cup C_2.$
worked_solution:
Let $C = C_1\cup C_2$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation. 

For line integrals with respect to $x,$ we have the following properties:

- $\displaystyle\int_{-C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = -\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

- $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = \int_{C_1} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x + \int_{C_2} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

In our case, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & =-(-2)-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & =2-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 6 & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\int_{-C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x = -6.
$$
